page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The instance is provisioned with 1344.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory density of 84.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX64-16ms_v2 demonstrates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2364.0 and a text processing score of 2950.0, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded operations are further validated by a gzip compression rate of 34.83 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.28 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13643.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 17775.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1381.43 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 131.84 GB/sec and 91.25 GB/sec, respectively. For database operations, the instance achieves an average of 25.14 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64-16ms_v2 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, allowing massive datasets to be retained in-memory without the overhead of scaling out to larger vCPU counts. However, the lack of local storage means that all persistent storage operations must rely on network-attached Premium Storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs compared to local NVMe SSDs. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel training, though its AMX support enables moderate CPU-based AI inference, as shown by a text generation speed of 282.43 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and enterprise software compilation.

It features 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, translating to 84.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. While the instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, it supports Premium Storage and advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks reveal top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2364.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics remain in the average tier, with Redis performance reaching 25.14 million SET operations per second. This profile is highly suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large in-memory databases, and caching layers that require massive RAM capacity relative to compute cores.
